messages:
maria: quick heads-up — I ran a perf sweep comparing FlashAttention-v2, paged-attn, and the fused kernel for the 13B model at seq_len=1024. KV cache was enabled for all runs. CSV uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/13B-attn-sweep-1774567890.csv :file_folder:

maria: TL;DR numbers (single A100-80GB, steady-state streaming perf, continuous batching enabled):
- FlashAttention-v2: ~4.2k tokens/sec, p50=18ms, p95=60ms, ~ $0.42 /M tokens
- fused-attn: ~3.7k tokens/sec, p50=16ms, p95=72ms, ~ $0.48 /M tokens
- paged-attn (KV optimized): ~3.0k tokens/sec, p50=22ms, p95=90ms, ~ $0.62 /M tokens

maria: note: when prefix reuse is high (KV cache hit ~70%), paged-attn throughput for multi-turn generation improved ~2.1x vs cold start, closing the gap with flash for long-lived sessions.

jack: nice — can you share how you computed $/M? and what's the batching config?

maria: cost calc = (gpu_hour_cost) / (tokens/sec * 3600) * 1e6. used our spot A100 rate of $2.5/hr for the sweep. batching: dynamic continuous batching with max_batch=32, max_latency_ms=12. KV cache kept in GPU memory.

cheng: curious about kernel-selection rules. did you force kernels or let the runtime pick? any regression triggers?

maria: forced for the sweep to isolate kernels. we also ran an automated selector run where runtime picked kernels based on seq_len and cached_hit_rate; selector picked flash for warm long seqs, fused for short seqs <256, paged when cache hit high and session length >> single request.

maria: pasted quick pseudo selector we used:
```
# kernel selector (simplified)
if seq_len <= 256:
    use = 'fused-attn'
elif kv_cache_hit_rate >= 0.6 and session_turns >= 4:
    use = 'paged-attn'
else:
    use = 'flash-v2'
```

sam: saw something weird — FlashAttention-v2 drops ~15% tokens/sec on CUDA 12.3 + cuBLAS 11.13 vs CUDA 11.8 in my local runs. did you pin driver/kernel?

maria: good catch. sweep was on CUDA 11.8 (driver 525). I’ll re-run a subset on 12.x; I suspect kernel codepaths and fused kernel launch config are sensitive.

perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1774567890/flash-v2-cold-vs-warm.nsftrace

elena: were these numbers with per-request prefix caching disabled or enabled? i.e., continuous vs one-off requests matters for latency distribution.

maria: continuous prefix caching enabled (simulates chat sessions). for one-off calls (no reuse) flash-v2 still wins on raw tokens/sec, but paged-attn latency tail is better for repeated incremental decode when KV hit rate >60%.

jack: can you paste the sample cost calc for flash?

maria: sample calc: tokens/sec=4200, gpu rate=$2.5/hr -> tokens/hr=15,120,000 -> $/M = 2.5 / 15.12 ≈ $0.165. but this assumes full GPU dedicated to that workload; our practical $/M above included multi-tenancy overhead and network/op costs so ~ $0.42 after amortization.

cheng: suggestion: route by (seq_len, prefix_reuse_score). small seq & low reuse -> fused; long seq & low reuse -> flash; long seq & high reuse -> paged. keep a safety Fallback: if p95 increases > x% switch kernels.

maria: agreed. propose thresholds: seq_len_threshold=256, reuse_threshold=0.5, p95_regress_threshold=30%. I'll add these to the selector config and run an A/B canary in staging.

infra-bot: canary flag created: feature/kernel-selector-thresholds, rollout=10% -> 1774568000

sam: also add an automated probe for CUDA/driver permutations — we should block kernel selection if we detect known perf regressions on 12.x.

maria: next steps:
- run 24h steady workload with selector enabled (10% canary)
- rerun flash-v2 subset on CUDA 12.x to confirm regression
- run quantized 4-bit variant to measure tokens/sec and cost delta
- add perf traces to nightly regression alerting

elena: sounds good. pls post final canary results in #eng-runtime and tag me.

jack: thanks — this helps the cost model work. any chance to run a small mixed workload (chat + embeddings) to see routing interactions?

maria: plan to include a mixed workload in the 24h run. will capture token mix and per-model $/M by route.

maria: ok i’ll kick off the CUDA 12 check and the 24h canary tomorrow. if anyone wants early access to the CSV/traces ping me. :eyes: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
